tools.name: connect_start
tools.description: Begin authentication. Send the user's work email; Victano mails them a six-digit code valid for 15 minutes and returns a request_id. Ask the user for the code, then call connect_verify with both. Nothing is charged and no card is needed.

tools.name: connect_verify
tools.description: Complete authentication with the request_id from connect_start and the six-digit code the user received. On success this session is authenticated immediately, with no reconnect, and the full toolset appears. Save the returned api_key into this client's MCP config as an Authorization: Bearer header s

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The connected account, its tier, how much quota remains in the current window, and how fresh the corpus is. Call this when a user asks about limits, or when you are unsure whether you are authenticated.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: The playbook library: how bid professionals actually run this work, from the weekly scan through qualification, eligibility screening, reading a specification, clarification questions, and the proposal skeleton. tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: The complete step-by-step playbook for one workflow id, including the decision gates, the EU procurement specifics that decide eligibility, and the pitfalls that lose bids. Follow it rather than summarising it.

tools.name: search_opportunities
tools.description: Hybrid keyword and semantic search across the corpus, with filters pushed into the scan. tools.name: get_opportunity
tools.description: The complete normalised record plus the document inventory. Use this before advising on a bid; a search card is not enough. Follow with read_document for the text that actually decides eligibility and scoring.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "connect_verify" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
